clips.text: Start with the cylinder block, the large body with three round holes. Place it in the main engine work area.
Place the smaller needle bearing in its matching round recess on the open crankcase side.
Place the larger needle bearing in its matching round recess on the open crankcase side.
Fit each curved upper main-bearing shell into a matching crankshaft support. Keep its bearing surface facing the crankshaft.
Fit the crankshaft into the open underside of the block. Its smooth round sections rest in the bearings you just placed.
Start the piston in its separate work area. The wide, flat piston top will face the cylinder head; the holes through its sides hold the wrist pin.
Place the narrow end of the connecting rod between the two supports inside the piston. Line up all three holes for the wrist pin.
Slide the wrist pin through the piston and the narrow end of the connecting rod. Add the retaining clips afterward so the pin cannot slide out.
Fit one wrist-pin circlip into the groove at each end of the pin. These two small clips stop the pin sliding out.
Fit the two threaded studs into the wide end of the connecting rod. Leave the separate rod cap off until the piston is in the engine.
Fit the oil-control ring into the lowest groove around the piston, nearest the connecting rod.
Fit the second compression ring into the middle groove around the piston.
Fit the top compression ring into the groove nearest the flat top of the piston.
Fit the complete piston units into the three cylinder bores. Keep their flat tops facing the cylinder head and guide each connecting rod toward the crankshaft.
From underneath the block, fit each rod cap to its connecting rod. Together they surround the smooth round section of the crankshaft.
Fit two nuts onto the studs of each rod cap. Finish all three caps before moving on.
Fit the four curved lower bearing shells into their matching supports underneath the crankshaft.
Fit the bedplate, the large lower support frame, to the underside of the block. It closes over the crankshaft bearing supports.
Fit the long M10 bedplate bolts into their matching holes around the lower support frame.
Fit the shorter M8 bedplate bolts into their matching holes around the lower support frame.
Start the oil sump in its separate work area. This is the large bowl underneath the engine; its open side faces the engine.
Place the flat baffle plate inside the oil sump. Line up its four screw holes with the small supports inside the bowl.
Fit the four baffle screws into the aligned holes inside the sump. The sump and baffle are now one complete unit.
Fit the complete sump-and-baffle unit underneath the bedplate. Its open side closes against the engine.
Fit the large M16 bolt into its matching opening on the installed sump.
Fit the short M8 by 30 bolt into its matching sump hole.
Fit the M8 by 35 bolts into their matching sump holes.
Fit the M8 by 40 bolt into its matching sump hole.
Fit the M8 by 45 bolt into its matching sump hole.
Fit the long M8 by 80 bolts into their matching sump holes.
Fit the flywheel, the large round disc, onto the crankshaft end opposite the timing-belt end.
Place the flywheel retaining plate over the centre of the flywheel. Line up the bolt holes.
Fit the six bolts through the retaining plate to secure the flywheel.
Start the cylinder head in its separate work area. Its underside has three combustion chambers; each chamber has four valve positions.
Slide each exhaust valve stem through its guide from the combustion-chamber side. Keep the wide valve face inside the chamber.
Slide each intake valve stem through its guide from the combustion-chamber side. Keep the wide valve face inside the chamber.
Fit the spring seat, the thin ring, around the raised valve-guide tube.
Slide the small stem seal over the valve stem. It rests inside the spring seat.
Slide the spring over the valve stem. Its lower end rests on the spring seat.
Place the cap-shaped retainer on top of the spring. The keepers will lock it to the stem.
Fit both tiny keeper halves into the groove near the top of the valve stem, on opposite sides. They lock the retainer in place.
Move the completed cylinder head onto the top of the cylinder block. Line up its three chambers with the three cylinder holes.
Fit the eight long head bolts through the head and into the block below it.
Fit the eight camshaft needle bearings into the supports along the top of the cylinder head.
Lay the exhaust camshaft in its bearings above the exhaust-valve row.
Lay the intake camshaft in its bearings above the intake-valve row.
Fit the front engine cover at the timing-belt end of the block. This is the end opposite the flywheel.
Fit a small pulley key into the slot at the end of each camshaft. The key keeps the pulley hub from turning on its shaft.
Slide each pulley hub onto its camshaft end. Line up the slot inside the hub with the key you just fitted.
Place a washer inside each camshaft pulley hub. These washers must go in before the hub bolts or outer pulleys.
Fit a bolt through each seated washer to secure the two camshaft pulley hubs.
Fit the crankshaft pulley key into the slot at the timing-belt end of the crankshaft.
Fit each camshaft timing pulley onto its secured hub.
Fit the crankshaft pulley onto the keyed end of the crankshaft.
Place the crankshaft pulley washer over the shaft end, against the outer face of the pulley.
Fit the outer pulley bolts into their matching camshaft-pulley holes.
Fit the large M22 nut onto the crankshaft pulley end.
Fit the timing-idler mounting plate beside the timing pulleys. It supports the two small belt-guide pulleys.
Fit the four screws through the timing-idler mounting plate.
Fit the two idler shafts into the mounting plate. Each shaft will carry one small belt-guide pulley.
Fit one inner circlip onto each idler shaft, in the groove closest to the mounting plate. Fit these before the idler units.
Start timing idler 1 in its separate work area. Place the small pulley with its centre hole ready for the bearings.
Fit both ball bearings into the centre hole of timing idler 1.
Fit the two retaining circlips into the grooves inside timing idler 1. They hold its bearings in place.
Start timing idler 2 in its separate work area. Place the small pulley with its centre hole ready for the bearings.
Fit both ball bearings into the centre hole of timing idler 2.
Fit the two retaining circlips into the grooves inside timing idler 2. They hold its bearings in place.
Slide each complete timing-idler unit onto its matching shaft, until it reaches the inner circlip already on the shaft.
Fit an outer circlip into the exposed groove on each shaft. These clips stop the complete idlers sliding off.
Fit the timing belt around the crankshaft pulley, the two camshaft pulleys, and the two timing idlers. The timing belt links the crankshaft and camshafts.
Fit the cylinder-head cover over the camshafts on top of the head.
Fit the cover bolts into the holes around the edge of the cylinder-head cover.
Fit one fuel injector into each of the three injector openings in the cylinder head.
Place the fuel rail across the tops of the three injectors. Its three connections line up with them.
Fit the two screws that hold the fuel rail in place.
Fit the fuel return line onto its fuel-system connection.
Fit the crankcase breather housing onto its mounting face. The breather lets gas leave the crankcase.
Fit the two screws through the breather housing.
Connect the breather hose between its two matching ports.
Fit the combined exhaust-manifold and turbocharger housing to the exhaust side of the cylinder head.
Fit the four screws through the exhaust-manifold mounting holes.
Fit the two turbo-shaft bearings inside the turbocharger housing.
Slide the turbo rotor shaft through the two bearings inside the housing.
Fit the two small retaining circlips into their grooves on the turbo shaft.
Fit the compressor wheel onto the air-intake end of the turbo shaft.
Fit the turbine wheel onto the exhaust end of the turbo shaft.
Fit the two M4 fasteners that hold the turbo wheels on the shaft.
Fit the exhaust outlet and catalyst housing to the exhaust side of the turbocharger.
Place the band clamp around the joint between the turbocharger and the exhaust outlet. Fit the clamp before its bolt.
Fit the M8 bolt into the turbo outlet clamp after the clamp is in place.
Fit the intake manifold to the intake side of the cylinder head. Its openings line up with the intake ports.
Fit the intake pipe connection into its matching intake opening.
Fit the intake pipe union at the next matching intake opening.
Fit the external service tube between its matching connections along the engine.
Fit the upper accessory mounting bracket to the engine first. It is the support above the lower bracket.
Fit the lower accessory mounting bracket below the upper bracket you just placed.
Fit spacer A into its matching accessory bracket position.
Fit spacer B into its matching accessory bracket position.
Fit the alternator onto its matching mounting supports.
Fit the starter motor onto its matching mounting supports.
Fit the alternator pulley onto the end of the alternator shaft.
Fit the accessory-idler shaft into its support. This shaft carries the small accessory-belt guide pulley.
Fit the inner shaft circlip into the groove nearest the support. It goes on before the complete accessory idler.
Start the accessory idler in its separate work area. Place the small pulley with its centre hole ready for the bearings.
Fit both ball bearings into the centre hole of the accessory-idler pulley.
Fit both retaining circlips into the grooves inside the accessory idler. They hold its bearings in place.
Slide the complete accessory idler onto its shaft until it meets the inner circlip.
Fit the outer shaft circlip into the exposed groove to stop the accessory idler sliding off.
Fit the complete motor unit onto its supports. Its internal parts stay together as one assembly item.
Fit the two motor mounting bolts through the supports.
Fit the two motor mounting nuts onto the bolts you just placed.
Fit the accessory drive belt around its matching pulleys to finish the engine. The engine assembly is complete.

Replace one faulty bearing while keeping the reusable parts. A circlip is a small split retaining ring that fits in a groove. The shaft rings keep the pulley on its support; the bore rings keep the bearings inside the pulley. Follow the labelled parts in this order.
Find the toothed timing belt around the pulleys at the timing end. Pick up the belt and press G to set it on the parts table.
Find timing idler 1, the small guide pulley. Remove the split retaining ring at its exposed shaft end and press G. Leave the ring behind the pulley fitted.
Pull timing idler 1 off its shaft as a complete unit. Press G to put it on the small work platform.
At the small platform, find the split ring inside the pulley opening. Remove the first labelled ring and press G. These two rings hold the bearings inside the pulley.
Remove the second labelled ring from the pulley opening and press G. Both bearing-retaining rings are now on the parts table.
Remove the outer idler bearing to reach the faulty inner bearing. Press G to set it aside for reuse.
Remove the faulty inner idler bearing. Press G to discard it from this repair; use the new replacement bearing next.
Pick up the part labelled New replacement · timing idler bearing from the table. Fit it into the empty inner bearing position inside the pulley.
Refit the original outer bearing into the remaining idler bearing seat.
Return the first labelled split ring to its groove inside the pulley opening. It keeps the bearing from sliding out.
Return the second labelled split ring to the other groove. Both bearings are retained, and the idler unit is complete again.
Pick up the rebuilt timing idler and fit it back onto its shaft, against the retained inner shaft circlip.
Refit the outer shaft circlip to secure the rebuilt idler.
Refit the timing belt around its original pulleys and idlers to complete the repair.
Chapter complete. Your section is assembled. Continue to the next chapter when you are ready.
Repair complete. The replacement bearing is fitted and the timing drive is rebuilt.
Turn the active workpiece upright before fitting the next part. Press F, or press the flip button beside its lift.
Turn the active workpiece upside down before fitting the next part. Press F, or press the flip button beside its lift.
You can carry several matching parts together. Pick them up one at a time, then place each at its highlighted position.
Build the remaining piston units using the same steps.
Repeat this fitting step for the remaining matching valve parts.
Repeat this step for the remaining matching parts.
